title: Field playbook: segment synopses & messaging pivots
content:
Purpose: quick, field-ready synopses for SDRs, AEs, and solutions engineers to land early-stage positioning across five priority verticals. This is intentionally lean — one pager per vertical plus proposed rapid experiments. Use as conversation scaffolding, not final legal/compliance copy.

TL;DR:
- Core claim: Redwood reduces inference cost per productive token while keeping predictable latency and enterprise-grade controls.
- Message pivots by vertical: fintech => unit economics + auditability; healthcare => PHI-safe private deployments + verified latency; legal => accurate context window handling + evidence traceability; enterprise SaaS => integration velocity + multitenancy controls; gov/defense => isolation, FIPS/KMS/HSM, and air-gap packaging.
- Primary proof points to reuse: dedicated capacity benchmarks, cached-prefix latency reductions, rollouts/canary success stories (internal case IDs available in linked artifacts).

How to use this doc:
- SDRs: pick 1–2 vertical lines under "core pitch" and one proof point. Keep convo under 3 min.
- AEs/SEs: use "pilot checklist" and "anchor metrics" when building proposals.
- Product/Marketing: these are hypotheses — run the experiments below and feed results back into central playbook.

1) Fintech (payments, neo-banks, lending platforms)
Primary pain: unpredictable per-request costs, burst throughput on payday cycles, auditability and data residency constraints.
Anchor metrics: avg cost per 100k generated tokens; p95 latency under 350ms for short queries; time-to-compliance (days to onboard to Dedicated/VPC).
Competitive signals: customers often trade off model fidelity vs cost; competitors pitching simple hosted APIs (cheaper short-term) but lack enterprise routing/fallback policies.
Core pitch: "Serve mission-critical inference with bank-grade predictability — Redwood gives you reserved throughput plus intelligent fallback and audit trails so compliance teams can sign off without rebuilding models in-house."
Risk & objections: "We run models ourselves" -> emphasize total cost of ownership and reliability blitz; "Vendor lock-in" -> call out consistent API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
Experiment ideas: A/B test two email subject lines: (A) "Reduce inference TCO for peak days" vs (B) "Signoff-ready inference for regulated finance". Pilot with 8 mid-market fintech prospect accounts.
Pilot checklist: SLA template, SOC2 extract, sample cost breakdown for 3 realistic traffic profiles.

2) Healthcare (telemedicine, clinical summarization, imaging notes workflows)
Primary pain: PHI exposure, audits, and deterministic latency for EHR flows.
Anchor metrics: HIPAA-ready private deployment checklist completed; mean latency under 500ms end-to-end for triage workflows; queueing fallback behavior documented.
Competitive signals: buying committee includes security/compliance execs; open-source solutions attractive but integration heavy.
Core pitch: "Plug Redwood into your EHR pipeline with private control plane and KMS/HSM key integration so clinicians get fast, auditable outputs without PHI leakage risk."
Risk & objections: clinical validation concerns -> propose scoped pilot with small non-production dataset and curated evals.
Experiment ideas: Run a controlled pilot with a health-tech incubator partner and capture clinical eval metrics; test two messages on a compliance audience: privacy-first vs speed-first.
Pilot checklist: Data flow diagram, privacy posture doc, dedicated onboarding engineer slot.

3) Legal (document review, contract analytics, eDiscovery tools)
Primary pain: need for provenance, hallucination risk minimization, long-context handling.
Anchor metrics: evidence traceability primitives (token-level provenance) shown; effective retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improvements measured by F1 on sample tasks.
Competitive signals: legal tech vendors prioritize accuracy and defensibility; hosted blackbox APIs are often rejected.
Core pitch: "Redwood helps reduce review time while preserving an auditable chain — private deployments and cached context reduce cost and control hallucinations via deterministic reranking policies."
Risk & objections: defenses about hallucinations -> share eval framework and prompt/regression monitoring examples.
Experiment ideas: Create a short RFP response template emphasizing auditability and run with two pilot counsel contacts.
Pilot checklist: sample RAG architecture diagram, hallucination audit plan, estimated throughput/cost for a 1M-doc corpus.

4) Enterprise SaaS (B2B product teams adding LLM features)
Primary pain: integration velocity, predictable billing for product usage, multi-tenant isolation.
Anchor metrics: token cost per MAU cohort; integration time from PoC to prod (target <6 weeks); route-level tracing in console.
Competitive signals: platform teams want SDKs, clear rollback policies, and tenant-level quotas.
Core pitch: "Ship LLM features faster with predictable economics: SDKs, detailed per-route cost telemetry, and canary rollouts that let you experiment without monetization risk."
Risk & objections: "We can build internal infra" -> use developer experience and observability demos as rebuttal.
Experiment ideas: Run a webinar + hands-on workshop that demos rapid integration using our SDK and shows cost telemetry. Measure conversion from attendees to trial provisioning.
Pilot checklist: SDK quickstart, sample tenant isolation config, billing preview template.

5) Gov / Defense (civil agencies, defense contractors)
Primary pain: isolation, certified crypto/KMS, air-gapped or on-prem packaging, export/compliance constraints.
Anchor metrics: FIPS-validated components, days-to-deploy on prem with provided ops runbook, successfully completed security questionnaire.
Competitive signals: procurement cycles long, emphasis on proven controls and vendor support model.
Core pitch: "Redwood offers deployable private control plane patterns and HSM integrations that align with agency security requirements — we focus on deterministic behavior and deep operational handoff."
Risk & objections: long procurement + C&A timelines -> propose gated onboarding plan with SRE/SEC shadowing.
Experiment ideas: Build a two-page vendor readiness datasheet tailored to FedRAMP-style questions and run it by three existing partner PMs for feedback.
Pilot checklist: export-control review, on-prem installer checklist, dedicated security review meeting cadences.

Cross-vertical message scaffolds (short lines):
- Value-first: "Cut inference costs and keep latency predictable so you can ship LLM features without budget surprises."
- Compliance-first: "Private control planes, KMS/HSM, and audit trails so security teams can approve quickly."
- Developer-first: "Same API for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — no rewrite as you scale."

Rapid experiment framework (what to measure):
- Signal conversion: reply rate to targeted outreach, MQL->SQL conversion for pilots.
- Technical validation: p95 latency, cost per 100k tokens, integration time.
- Compliance lift: number of security requirements satisfied in first pass.
- Qualitative: prospect quotes on top 3 buying criteria.

A/B testing cookbook (examples):
- Subject line test (Fintech): economics vs compliance angle. Measure reply rate over 2 weeks, n>=200.
- Deck opener (Enterprise SaaS): demo-first vs metrics-first. Measure meeting booked rate.
- Pilot offer (Healthcare): sandbox dataset vs dry-run eval. Measure acceptance rate.

Next steps & owners:
- Run subject-line fintech A/B with Ben (owner) by 2026-03-10.
- Draft healthcare pilot template and privacy checklist (Maya) by 2026-03-20.
- Create legal RFP boilerplate and hallucination audit guide (Ethan) by 2026-03-22.
- Product: add two per-route telemetry screenshots to the sales playbook (Priya) by 2026-03-15.

Notes / open questions:
- Should we surface a simplified cost estimator on the public site tailored to fintech traffic profiles? (cost of maintaining example datasets + dedicated capacity options)
- Which existing Dedicated case studies are okay to reference externally? Need comms signoff.

Appendix: quick rebuttal kernels (copy these into notes)
- "We run models ourselves" -> "Totally — many customers do a hybrid approach. Redwood reduces ops overhead and gives you fallbacks, predictable unit economics, and faster upgrades without re-architecting inference paths."
- "Blackbox API risk" -> "We provide Private deployments and per-token provenance tracing for sensitive workloads; we also support on-prem installer packages for air-gapped environments."

End — feedback welcome. Mark comments inline in doc or ping owners on Slack #gtm-verticals.
